I'm confirming the status enum maps correctly between integer and string forms for export/import, and deciding bundles can stay as a direct faithful copy. Now I'm turning to the user record set, noting the export adds an email address field while import handles rows that lack an identity_id for deferred linking, and starting to write out the full data_transfer layer beginning with the base RecordSet.

Writing the RecordSet class...

I realize I need `each_file` to yield Entry objects rather than path strings, since looking up entries by path for every file would turn reading into an O(n²) operation across millions of entries. So callbacks receive `entry.path` as `file:`, while internal methods like `check_record` read directly from the Entry. I'm also thinking conflict checks should be batched per slice rather than done per-record, to avoid issuing one query per file.

I'm sketching a shared pipeline: `load_rows(entries)` parses and validates, then `check` calls `check_conflicts(rows)` while `import` calls `check_references(rows)` followed by `insert(rows)`. Conflict checking becomes a single existence query against the batch of ids rather than per-record lookups, since every manifest model has an id.

I'm also defining an error hierarchy under `Account::DataTransfer`, separating malformed/inconsistent data (`IntegrityError`) from already-existing data on the instance (`ConflictError`), and considering where in the model files these should live.

Working out the Zeitwerk implications: `Account::DataTransfer` is currently an implicit namespace auto-generated from the directory structure, so adding an explicit file defining the module should work cleanly, and the nested `ActiveStorage`/`ActionText` namespaces inside it need fully-qualified `::ActiveStorage::Blob` references to avoid clashing with the real gems. Now I'm writing the `load(entry)` method that reads a zip entry, parses it as JSON with UTF-8 encoding, and rescues parsing errors.

I also need an `check_id` method validating that each entry's id matches the expected format and that the filename matches the id, plus I'm realizing I need to bound-check that a 25-character base36 id doesn't exceed 2^128, since base36's max range can slightly exceed that threshold.

I'm extending the same validation approach to every UUID-typed foreign key column, checking the adapter's type mapping to identify which columns are UUIDs and allowing nil only when the column is nullable. Then I'm writing a row-building helper that maps each attribute to its data value or a default when missing.

Now I'm moving to reference validation during import—grouping rows by polymorphic type to check existence per type, filtering out rows with blank IDs before checking existence, and I'm considering the edge case where a polymorphic type is nil but an ID is still present.

I'm thinking through how to safely resolve a polymorphic type string to a class without risking arbitrary constant loading, considering whether to restrict it to a known set of models from the manifest rather than freely constantizing the string.

I'll use an explicit whitelist of allowed polymorphic types (Account, Board, Card, Comment, Event, Mention, User, ActionText::RichText, ActiveStorage::Blob, ActiveStorage::VariantRecord) and only constantize if the type matches one of these, raising an integrity error otherwise. I also need to account for special cases per subclass—skipping global references like identity for users, remapping the container account for entropy records, and handling attachment records that can point to either blobs or variant records.

I'm verifying that existence checks scope correctly by account_id for Blob, RichText, and VariantRecord, that count queries can rely on primary key indexes for performance, and that insert_all! will correctly raise on duplicate records during import.

I'm confirming insert_all! bypasses callbacks and scope attributes, so no stray Searchable or Storage entries get created and reconciliation happens afterward separately. For rich texts I'm handling sgid/gid conversion with account checks on import, and for blobs I'm making sure service_name is excluded on export and reassigned appropriately on import.

For attachments I'm excluding internal record types during export. For file export, I'm reconsidering the zip-writing approach—streaming blob contents directly into the zip risks leaving a corrupted entry if the download fails partway, so I'm leaning toward checking blob existence first via the service before attempting to write it, accepting the extra HEAD request as a reasonable tradeoff.

On compression, I'm deciding to just use stored (uncompressed) entries for everything rather than selectively deflating text files, since the complexity isn't worth the marginal savings.

For import, I'm matching each zip entry's key to a blob record scoped to the account, raising an integrity error if no match is found or if the file size doesn't match the blob's recorded byte size, then uploading the entry's contents back to the storage service using the blob's key and checksum.

I'm noting that the disk service's checksum verification will catch mismatches automatically, deleting the bad file and raising an integrity error I can translate into my own exception type. For the validation-only pass, I'm concluding it's simplest to just check key formatting since the actual blob metadata lives inside JSON files rather than being derivable from the zip entry names, and I'm now moving on to how the Account subclass should export its own JSON file.

For account import I'll update the name, join code, and cards count. For users, export now needs the email address, but I'm deferring identity linking until after the main import completes -- stripping identity_id during row import and resolving it at the end by rereading each user JSON file to pair user IDs with emails. I'm sketching out a completion step that iterates the zip's user entries, loads each one, and checks whether there's an email address to link an identity to, while skipping deactivated users.

Since deactivating a user already clears its identity, those records should have no email address, so they're naturally skipped. For identities that don't already exist, I need to track which ones get freshly created so they can be rolled back if the import fails later -- meaning identity linking should be one of the last fallible steps, happening after reindexing and storage reconciliation but before marking the import complete.

I also want to confirm identities need to be created at all for imported users: without one, those users couldn't sign in via magic link later, since there's no mechanism to retroactively attach an identity to an existing user record when someone rejoins with the same email. So creating identities during import is necessary to preserve access.

There's a mild security concern worth flagging: creating identities for arbitrary imported emails means an attacker-controlled account could show up in a victim's account list when they sign in, since no invite confirmation step is involved here—unlike normal invites that require clicking a join link. It seems like a minor, pre-existing tradeoff rather than something new to fix, and no email gets sent to imported users either way.

Setting up the importer as owner...

I'm reconsidering whether to even create the signup users at all. If I use Signup#complete to create both the billing account and the owner account, that works for both OSS and SaaS cases—then at import start I just delete the placeholder owner and system users. I still need to figure out where the owner's name comes from (derived from the identity or email), and on completion check whether the importer itself was among the imported users.

Then there's the single-tenant OSS case: `Account.accepting_signups?` blocks new signups once an account exists, which conflicts with imports needing to create a new account. For a fresh OSS install with zero accounts, the typical flow is importing the SaaS export as the very first account—but reaching the import page requires being signed in, which raises the question of how sign-in works before any account exists.

So the answer is: signing up creates an identity via magic link (allowed since `Account.none?`), then instead of completing signup, the user can jump to `/account/imports/new`. That means import access should be gated by `Account.accepting_signups?` in single-tenant mode (no accounts yet) but always allowed in multi-tenant mode, enforced in the imports controller similar to the signup controller's tenant-limit check, with links to import placed on the signup completion page and in the session menu when signups are open.

I'm also checking edge cases: a failed import destroys the created account, restoring `Account.none?` so a retry is possible; an in-progress import blocks a second attempt since `Account.none?` becomes false, which is the desired behavior.     def limit_reached_for?(user)
      where(user: user).recent.count >= DAILY_LIMIT
    end
  end

  end

    processing!

  end

    completed? && expires_at.past?

steps.reasoning_content:
I realize the default rescue behavior would resume the job on error after advancing, but for a mid-import failure I actually want it to fail and clean up rather than retry. So I'll catch errors myself within the steps before continuation's rescue sees them, then explicitly mark the import as failed.

But I need to be careful: if the cleanup call (`import.fail`) itself raises—say the DB is down—that exception would escape and trigger a resume, which could re-run the import into a half-cleaned state. That's a dangerous edge case I need to guard against, possibly by disabling resume-after-advancing entirely.

So I'll structure `fail` to mark the import as failed first, then run cleanup, then send the email, so even if cleanup errors out downstream, the failed status is already recorded and visible. I'm also considering making `perform` idempotent by returning immediately if the import is already completed or failed, and double-checking that checkpointing after each batch of 100 records correctly captures the cursor so interrupted jobs resume exactly where they left off.

I'm now worried about the edge case where a worker is killed hard right after committing a batch but before the cursor checkpoint runs — that leaves the job lost and the import stuck in "processing" forever. This points toward needing a recurring sweeper that marks stalled imports (processing with a stale updated_at) as failed, similar to an export cleanup task, so partial data never lingers indefinitely without resolution.

If SolidQueue fails claimed executions with ProcessPrunedError when a process is pruned, that's fine since the job stays failed and data gets cleaned up. But if it instead releases executions back to ready, a re-run would resume from the last serialized continuation, re-attempting batches already inserted and hitting conflicts — resulting in a misleading "already exists" failure even though the real cause was a crash.

Now I'm mapping exceptions to user-facing failure messages: ConflictError becomes a note that data may already be imported, IntegrityError surfaces the validation message, invalid or oversized ZIP archives get a damaged-file message, and missing or corrupted uploaded files get their own explanatory messages.

For anything unexpected, I fall back to a generic "something went wrong" message and report the error, storing the failure reason on the import and emailing it. I'm now defining the Account::Import model with its attachment, status enum (pending/processing/completed/failed), and a stalled scope that flags imports stuck in processing or pending too long.

I'm adding a class method to fail stalled imports, plus instance methods to queue processing later and to check the file by reading the zip and walking through each record set in the manifest, handling resume state via a start cursor so processing can continue from where it left off.

Then there's the actual import method that mirrors this, calling record_set.import per manifest entry, followed by a finish method that opens the file again inside a transaction to link user identities and set up the importer, then reconciles, reindexes, purges the file, marks the import completed, and sends a completion email. I'm now thinking through the correct ordering within finish—updating the account's cards_count before reindexing cards/comments in search.

Reindexing may need to be a separate step using a cursor by card/comment id rather than bundled into finish directly. So the job steps become: check, prepare (removing signup-created users), import, reindex (cursor-based), then finish handling storage reconciliation (boards and account), identity linking, importer setup, file purge, completion status, and email.

I'm weighing where "prepare" should happen—whether it belongs in the job before import, or could instead happen right in the controller when the account is created via Signup, since that's when the users are initially created.

The real question is whether it's wasteful to create a signup owner user just to delete it later. I'm considering instead adding a dedicated method on Signup specifically for imports, something like a `start` method on `Account::Import` that builds a Signup object tailored for this purpose rather than going through the normal completion flow.

But I'm also weighing whether the importer's own user should remain active as account owner during the import process, versus being removed. Keeping it creates risks—like email collisions when imported users overlap with the importer's identity, or stray data the importer creates while the import is still running—so deleting the signup user afterward, while awkward, might actually be the safer, cleaner path.

I'm checking that `account.users.destroy_all` cleanly cascades through comments, filters, pins, accesses, settings, and notifications without leaving orphaned records, and verifying no other account-level process (like entropy updates) depends on that system user still existing after destruction.

# Moves whole accounts in and out of Fizzy as ZIP archives (see Account::Export
# and Account::Import), so they can travel between Fizzy instances.
#
#   data/account.json           The account itself
#   data/<table>/<id>.json      One file per record, as listed in the Manifest
#   storage/<key>               The stored files, named after their blob keys
module Account::DataTransfer
  class Error < StandardError; end

  # The archive is damaged, or its data is not consistent.
  class IntegrityError < Error; end

  # The archive contains data that already exists in this Fizzy.
  class ConflictError < Error; end
end
EOF
cat > app/models/account/data_transfer/record_set.rb <<'EOF'
# Exports the records of a model into an archive, and checks and imports them back.
#
# Records keep their ids when imported, and are always imported into the target
# account. Before inserting each batch, every reference to another record is
# verified to point to a record that was already imported into the same account,
# so an archive can never be used to reach data in other accounts.
class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[ Export Account::Import ].freeze

  # Polymorphic references are only allowed to point to these models
  REFERENCEABLE_TYPES = %w[
    Account Board Card Comment Event Mention User
    ActionText::RichText ActiveStorage::Blob ActiveStorage::VariantRecord
  ].freeze

  BATCH_SIZE = 100
  ID_FORMAT = /\A[0-9a-z]{25}\z/
  MAX_ID = 2**128

  attr_reader :account, :model, :attributes

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil)
    @account = account
    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
  end

  # Identifies the record set in the cursors used to resume imports
  def name
    model_dir
  end

  def export(to:)
    with_zip(to) do
      each_record { |record| export_record(record) }
    end
  end

  # Validates the records in the archive without importing anything.
  def check(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      each_batch(start: start) do |entries|
        check_batch(entries)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: entries.last.path)
      end
    end
  end

  def import(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      each_batch(start: start) do |entries|
        model.transaction { import_batch(entries) }
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: entries.last.path)
      end
    end
  end

  # Deletes everything of this kind in the account, to roll back a failed import.
  def delete_all
    records.in_batches(of: 1000).delete_all
  end

  private
    attr_reader :zip

    def with_zip(zip)
      old_zip = @zip
      @zip = zip
      yield
    ensure
      @zip = old_zip
    end

    def records
      model.where(account_id: account.id)
    end

    def model_dir
      model.table_name
    end

    # Exporting

    def each_record(&block)
      if records.respond_to?(:find_each)
        records.find_each(&block)
      else
        records.each(&block)
      end
    end

    def export_record(record)
      zip.add_file "data/#{model_dir}/#{record.id}.json", serialize(record).to_json
    end

    def serialize(record)
      record.attributes.slice(*attributes).transform_values do |value|
        value.respond_to?(:utc) ? value.utc.iso8601(6) : value
      end
    end

    # Importing

    def files
      zip.each_entry("data/#{model_dir}/*.json")
    end

    def each_batch(start:, &block)
      entries = files
      entries = entries_after(entries, start) if start
      entries.each_slice(BATCH_SIZE, &block)
    end

    def entries_after(entries, start)
      started = false

      Enumerator.new do |yielder|
        entries.each do |entry|
          if started
            yielder << entry
          else
            started = entry.path == start
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def check_batch(entries)
      check_conflicts entries.map { |entry| build_row(entry) }
    end

    def import_batch(entries)
      rows = entries.map { |entry| build_row(entry) }

      check_references(rows)
      insert(rows)
    end

    def build_row(entry)
      data = load(entry)
      check_id(data, entry)

      row_from(data).tap do |row|
        check_values(row, entry)
      end
    end

    def load(entry)
      data = JSON.parse(zip.read(entry).force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8))

      if data.is_a?(Hash)
        data
      else
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} doesn't contain a record"
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError, EncodingError
      raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} isn't valid JSON"
    end

    def entry_path(entry)
      entry.respond_to?(:path) ? entry.path : entry
    end

    def row_from(data)
      attributes.index_with { |attribute| data.key?(attribute) ? data[attribute] : default_value_for(attribute) }.tap do |row|
        row["account_id"] = account.id if row.key?("account_id")
      end
    end

    def default_value_for(attribute)
      if attribute.in?(%w[ created_at updated_at ])
        Time.current
      else
        model.column_defaults[attribute]
      end
    end

    def check_id(data, entry)
      unless valid_id?(data["id"]) && File.basename(entry_path(entry), ".json") == data["id"]
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} doesn't have a valid id"
      end
    end

    def valid_id?(value)
      value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(ID_FORMAT) && value.to_i(36) < MAX_ID
    end

    def check_values(row, entry)
      uuid_attributes.each do |attribute|
        unless row[attribute].nil? || valid_id?(row[attribute])
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} has an invalid #{attribute}"
        end
      end

      model.defined_enums.each do |attribute, mapping|
        value = row[attribute]

        unless value.nil? || mapping.key?(value.to_s) || mapping.value?(value)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} has an invalid #{attribute}"
        end
      end

      polymorphic_references.each do |reflection|
        type = row[reflection.foreign_type]

        unless type.nil? || type.in?(REFERENCEABLE_TYPES)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} references an unknown kind of record (#{type})"
        end
      end
    end

    def uuid_attributes
      @uuid_attributes ||= attributes.select do |attribute|
        model.type_for_attribute(attribute).is_a?(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid)
      end
    end

    def check_conflicts(rows)
      if model.where(id: rows.pluck("id")).exists?
        raise Account::DataTransfer::ConflictError, "#{model.model_name.human.pluralize} in this file already exist in this Fizzy"
      end
    end

    def references
      model.reflect_on_all_associations(:belongs_to).reject do |reflection|
        reflection.name == :account || skipped_references.include?(reflection.name)
      end
    end

    def skipped_references
      []
    end

    def polymorphic_references
      references.select(&:polymorphic?)
    end

    # Ensures that every record referenced by the rows belongs to the account being imported
    def check_references(rows)
      referenced_ids(rows).each do |klass, ids|
        ensure_imported(klass, ids)
      end
    end

    def referenced_ids(rows)
      Hash.new { |hash, klass| hash[klass] = Set.new }.tap do |referenced|
        references.each do |reflection|
          rows.each do |row|
            if id = row[reflection.foreign_key.to_s]
              klass = reflection.polymorphic? ? row[reflection.foreign_type].constantize : reflection.klass
              referenced[klass] << id
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def ensure_imported(klass, ids)
      found = if klass == Account
        ids.count { |id| id == account.id }
      else
        klass.where(account_id: account.id, id: ids.to_a).count
      end

      unless found == ids.size
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "Some #{model.model_name.human.pluralize.downcase} reference #{klass.model_name.human.pluralize.downcase} that aren't in the file"
      end
    end

    def insert(rows)
      model.insert_all!(rows) if rows.any?
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique
      raise Account::DataTransfer::ConflictError, "#{model.model_name.human.pluralize} in this file already exist in this Fizzy"
    rescue ActiveRecord::NotNullViolation, ActiveRecord::ValueTooLong, ActiveRecord::RangeError
      raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "Some #{model.model_name.human.pluralize.downcase} in this file are incomplete or invalid"
    end
end

# uncompressed: most of them are images and documents that are compressed already.

  def initialize(account)

  end

  end

      blob.service.delete(blob.key)
    end
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActiveStorage::Blob.where(account: account).where.not(id: excluded_blob_ids)
    end

    def excluded_blob_ids
      ::ActiveStorage::Attachment.where(account: account, record_type: INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES).select(:blob_id)
    end

    def export_record(blob)
      if blob.service.exist?(blob.key)
        zip.add_file("storage/#{blob.key}", compress: false) do |file|
          blob.download { |chunk| file.write(chunk) }
        end
      else
        Rails.logger.warn "[Export] Skipping missing file for blob #{blob.id} (#{blob.key})"
      end
    end

    def files
      zip.each_entry("storage/*")
    end

    def check_batch(entries)
      entries.each do |entry|
        unless File.basename(entry.path).match?(Account::DataTransfer::ActiveStorage::BlobRecordSet::KEY_FORMAT)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry.path} isn't a valid file name"
        end
      end
    end

    def import_batch(entries)
      blobs = records.where(key: entries.map { |entry| File.basename(entry.path) }).index_by(&:key)

      entries.each do |entry|
        if blob = blobs[File.basename(entry.path)]
          upload(blob, entry)
        else
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry.path} doesn't belong to any file in the account"
        end
      end
    end

    def upload(blob, entry)
      if entry.size == blob.byte_size
        zip.open(entry) do |io|
          blob.service.upload(blob.key, io, checksum: blob.checksum.presence)
        end
      else
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry.path} doesn't have the expected size"
      end
    rescue ActiveStorage::IntegrityError
      raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry.path} is damaged"
    end
end

# can only be verified by the Fizzy that signed them. They are exported as plain
# global ids instead, and signed again when imported, as long as they point to
# records of the account being imported.
class Account::DataTransfer::ActionText::RichTextRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  ATTACHABLE_TYPES = %w[ ActiveStorage::Blob User ].freeze

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: ::ActionText::RichText)
  end

  private
    def records
      ::ActionText::RichText.where(account: account)
    end

    def serialize(rich_text)
      super.merge("body" => exportable_body(rich_text.body&.to_html))
    end

    def row_from(data)
      super.merge("body" => importable_body(data["body"]))
    end

    def exportable_body(html)
      convert_attachments(html) do |node|
        if record = attachable_from_sgid(node["sgid"])
          node["gid"] = record.to_global_id.to_s
        end
      end
    end

    def importable_body(html)
      convert_attachments(html) do |node|
        if record = attachable_from_gid(node["gid"])
          node["sgid"] = record.attachable_sgid
        end
      end
    end

    def convert_attachments(html)
      if html.is_a?(String) && html.present?
        fragment = ::ActionText::HtmlConversion.fragment_for_html(html)

        fragment.css(::ActionText::Attachment.tag_name).each do |node|
          attributes = node.attributes.keys
          yield node.tap { node.remove_attribute("gid") }.dup.then { node } if false
          sgid, gid = node["sgid"], node["gid"]
          node.remove_attribute("sgid")
          node.remove_attribute("gid")
          node["sgid"], node["gid"] = sgid, gid
          yield node
          node.remove_attribute("sgid") if node["gid"] && attributes.include?("sgid")
          node.remove_attribute("gid") if node["sgid"] && attributes.include?("gid")
        end

        fragment.to_html
      else
        html
      end
    end

    def attachable_from_sgid(sgid)
      if sgid.present?
        record = GlobalID::Locator.locate_signed(sgid, for: ::ActionText::Attachable::LOCATOR_NAME)
        record if record.class.name.in?(ATTACHABLE_TYPES) && record.account_id == account.id
      end
    rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
      nil
    end

    def attachable_from_gid(gid)
      if (global_id = GlobalID.parse(gid.to_s)) && global_id.model_name.in?(ATTACHABLE_TYPES)
        global_id.model_name.constantize.find_by(account_id: account.id, id: global_id.model_id)
      end
    end
end

# Lists everything that makes up an account, in the order it must be imported:
# records only reference records that come before them.
class Account::DataTransfer::Manifest
  attr_reader :account

  def initialize(account)
    @account = account
  end

  # Yields each record set, along with the last file processed for it when
  # resuming from a cursor (an array with the name of a record set and a file).
  def each_record_set(start: nil)
    raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

    record_set_name, last_file = start

    record_sets_from(record_set_name).each do |record_set|
      yield record_set, (last_file if record_set.name == record_set_name)
    end
  end

  # Removes everything imported into the account, newest kinds of records first.
  def delete_all
    record_sets.reverse_each(&:delete_all)
  end

  private
    def record_sets_from(name)
      if name
        index = record_sets.index { |record_set| record_set.name == name } || raise(ArgumentError, "Unknown record set: #{name}")
        record_sets.drop(index)
      else
        record_sets
      end
    end

    def record_sets
      @record_sets ||= [
        Account::DataTransfer::AccountRecordSet.new(account),
        Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::User::Settings,
          ::Tag,
          ::Board,
          ::Column
        ),
        Account::DataTransfer::EntropyRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::Board::Publication,
          ::Webhook,
          ::Access,
          ::Card,
          ::Comment,
          ::Step,
          ::Assignment,
          ::Tagging,
          ::Closure,
          ::Card::Goldness,
          ::Card::NotNow,
          ::Card::ActivitySpike,
          ::Watch,
          ::Pin,
          ::Reaction,
          ::Mention
        ),
        Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet.new(account),
        record_set_for(::Webhook::DelinquencyTracker),
        Account::DataTransfer::EventRecordSet.new(account),
        *record_sets_for(
          ::Notification,

steps.reasoning_content:
I'm realizing the "No space left on device" error is happening because the export zip blob itself gets created in storage before it's attached to the Export record, so the exclusion logic that normally skips already-attached export blobs doesn't catch it yet—causing the export to try including itself.

I'm weighing fixes: either attach the blob to the record early (before streaming completes) so exclusion logic kicks in, purging on failure, or instead modifying the record set query to exclude pending/unattached blobs directly. The early-attach approach raises a concern though—attaching triggers an after-commit analyze job, which could try to download and inspect a partially-written file before the write finishes.

I'm checking that attaching early still works for the Export#build retry case since it purges any already-attached file first, and confirming the Account::Import blob follows the same excluded-attachment pattern. Then I'm weighing an alternative approach (d): building the export blob without persisting it until the upload completes, so for S3 I'd use a streaming upload keyed to the blob before creating the record.

I'm leaning toward this deferred-persistence approach — generate the blob's secure token key lazily, write the file, then only call `update!` with byte_size and checksum (which persists it) and attach once everything succeeds; on failure, delete the uploaded file from the service directly by key. This keeps a partial blob from ever being visible and sidesteps the analyze race condition, so I prefer this option.

Now let me rewrite the ZipFile.create_for_* methods accordingly.

I found the bug: the export zipped its own in-progress file since the blob wasn't yet excluded, causing it to recursively grow until the disk filled. I'll clean up now and fix it so the export's blob isn't persisted until the archive is fully complete.

class ZipFile
  class << self
    def create_for(attachment, filename:)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      reflection = attachment.record.class.reflect_on_attachment(attachment.name)
      service_name = reflection.options[:service_name] || ActiveStorage::Blob.service.name
      service = ActiveStorage::Blob.services.fetch(service_name)

      if s3_service?(service)
        create_for_s3(attachment, filename: filename, service: service) { |zip| yield zip }
      elsif disk_service?(service)
        create_for_disk(attachment, filename: filename, service: service) { |zip| yield zip }
      else
        create_for_tempfile(attachment, filename: filename) { |zip| yield zip }
      end
    end

    # Yields a ZipFile::Reader for the archive stored in the blob without downloading
    # it first: S3 objects are read with ranged requests, and files in disk services
    # are read in place. That way archives of any size can be read.
    def read_from(blob)
      raise ArgumentError, "No block given" unless block_given?

      if s3_service?(blob.service)
        read_from_s3(blob) { |zip| yield zip }
      elsif disk_service?(blob.service)
        read_from_disk(blob) { |zip| yield zip }
      else
        read_from_tempfile(blob) { |zip| yield zip }
      end
    end

    private
      def s3_service?(service)
        # The S3 service doesn't get loaded in development unless it's used
        defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::S3Service)
      end

      def disk_service?(service)
        defined?(ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService) && service.is_a?(ActiveStorage::Service::DiskService)
      end

      # The blob is only saved once the archive is complete, so that it can't be
      # mistaken for a regular file of the account while it's being written.
      def create_for_s3(attachment, filename:, service:)
        blob = build_blob(filename: filename, service: service)
        writer = Writer.new

        # Use S3's upload_stream directly for write-based streaming.
        # ActiveStorage's upload method expects a read-based IO, but ZipKit
        # needs a write-based stream. The TransferManager's upload_stream
        # yields a writable IO that we can stream directly to.
        service.send(:upload_stream,
          key: blob.key,
          content_type: "application/zip",
          part_size: 100.megabytes
        ) do |write_stream|
          write_stream.binmode
          writer.stream_to(write_stream)
          yield writer
          writer.close
        end

        complete(attachment, blob: blob, writer: writer)
      rescue Aws::S3::MultipartUploadError => e
        discard(blob, service: service)

        if e.errors.any?
          raise e.errors.first
        else
          raise e
        end
      rescue Exception
        discard(blob, service: service)
        raise
      end

      # Writes the archive straight into its final location in the disk service, so
      # that huge archives don't need as much free space again for a temporary copy.
      def create_for_disk(attachment, filename:, service:)
        blob = build_blob(filename: filename, service: service)
        path = service.path_for(blob.key)
        FileUtils.mkdir_p(File.dirname(path))

        writer = File.open(path, "wb") do |file|
          Writer.new(file).tap do |writer|
            yield writer
            writer.close
          end
        end

        complete(attachment, blob: blob, writer: writer)
      rescue Exception
        discard(blob, service: service)
        raise
      end

      def create_for_tempfile(attachment, filename:)
        tempfile = Tempfile.new([ "export", ".zip" ])
        tempfile.binmode

        writer = Writer.new(tempfile)
        yield writer
        writer.close

        tempfile.rewind
        attachment.attach(io: tempfile, filename: filename, content_type: "application/zip")
      ensure
        tempfile&.close
        tempfile&.unlink
      end

      def build_blob(filename:, service:)
        ActiveStorage::Blob.new(filename: filename, content_type: "application/zip", service_name: service.name).tap do |blob|
          blob.key # Generates the key
        end
      end

      def complete(attachment, blob:, writer:)
        blob.update!(byte_size: writer.byte_size, checksum: writer.checksum)
        attachment.attach(blob)
      end

      def discard(blob, service:)
        if blob
          blob.destroy if blob.persisted?
          service.delete(blob.key)
        end
      rescue => error
        Rails.error.report(error, severity: :warning)
      end

      def read_from_s3(blob)
        yield Reader.new(RemoteIO.new(blob))
      end

      def read_from_disk(blob)
        File.open(blob.service.path_for(blob.key), "rb") do |file|
          yield Reader.new(file)
        end
      end

      def read_from_tempfile(blob)
        blob.open do |file|
          yield Reader.new(file)
        end
      end
  end
end
EOF

# Imports an account export (see Account::Export) into a brand new account.
#
# The import runs in steps (see Account::ImportJob): the file is checked first,
# so most problems are caught before anything is written. Then the records and
# files are imported, the search index and storage totals are rebuilt and, at
# last, people are connected to their identities so they can sign in. Until
# then, nobody can access the new account.
#
# If anything goes wrong, everything imported is removed along with the new
# account, and the person importing gets an email explaining why.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  STALLED_AFTER = 1.hour
  PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 1.minute

  belongs_to :account, optional: true
  belongs_to :identity

  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  scope :in_progress, -> { where(status: %w[ pending processing ]) }
  scope :stalled, -> { in_progress.where(updated_at: ...STALLED_AFTER.ago) }

  validate :ensure_file_is_attached, on: :create

  class << self
    # Creates a new account for the identity and starts importing the file into it.
    def start(identity:, file:)
      signup = Signup.new(identity: identity, full_name: importer_name_for(identity), skip_account_seeding: true)

      if signup.complete
        create_for(signup.account, identity: identity, file: file).tap(&:process_later)
      else
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotSaved, signup.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
      end
    end

    def fail_stalled
      stalled.find_each do |import|
        import.fail Account::DataTransfer::Error.new("The import stopped making progress")
      end
    end

    def importer_name_for(identity)
      identity.users.where.not(name: identity.email_address).order(:updated_at).last&.name ||
        identity.email_address.split("@").first
    end

    private
      def create_for(account, identity:, file:)
        Current.with_account(account) do
          # Nobody can get into the account until it has been imported
          account.users.destroy_all
          create!(account: account, identity: identity, file: file)
        end
      rescue
        account.destroy
        raise
      end
  end

  def process_later
    Account::ImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def check(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing! if pending?

    each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, zip, last_file|
      record_set.check(from: zip, start: last_file, callback: progress_callback(callback))
    end
  end

  def import(start: nil, callback: nil)
    each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, zip, last_file|
      record_set.import(from: zip, start: last_file, callback: progress_callback(callback))
    end
  end

  def reindex(start: nil, callback: nil)
    reindex_cards(start: start, callback: callback)
    reindex_comments(start: start, callback: callback)
  end

  def finish
    Current.with_account(account) do
      reconcile_account
      connect_people

      file.purge
      update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
    end

    ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  end

  # Removes everything imported along with the new account, and lets the person
  # importing know why the import failed.
  def fail(error)
    update!(status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason_for(error))
    report(error)

    roll_back
    ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
  end

  def in_progress?
    pending? || processing?
  end

  private
    def ensure_file_is_attached
      errors.add(:file, "is missing") unless file.attached?
    end

    def manifest
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account)
    end

    def each_record_set(start: nil)
      Current.with_account(account) do
        read_file do |zip|
          manifest.each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_file|
            yield record_set, zip, last_file
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def read_file(&block)
      ZipFile.read_from(file.blob, &block)
    end

    # Reports the position of the import, so that it can be resumed from there if interrupted
    def progress_callback(callback)
      lambda do |record_set:, file:|
        touch if updated_at < PROGRESS_INTERVAL.ago
        callback&.call([ record_set.name, file ])
      end
    end

    def reindex_cards(start:, callback:)
      if start.nil? || start.first == "cards"
        account.cards.published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(start: start&.last) do |card|
          card.reindex
          callback&.call([ "cards", card.id ])
        end
      end
    end

    def reindex_comments(start:, callback:)
      comment_start = start&.last if start&.first == "comments"

      Comment.where(account: account).joins(:card).merge(Card.published).includes(:rich_text_body, :card).find_each(start: comment_start) do |comment|
        comment.reindex
        callback&.call([ "comments", comment.id ])
      end
    end

    def reconcile_account
      account.update!(cards_count: [ account.cards_count, account.cards.maximum(:number).to_i ].max)

      account.boards.find_each do |board|
        board.reconcile_storage
        board.materialize_storage
      end

      account.reconcile_storage
      account.materialize_storage
    end

    # Identities are global, so people are connected to them only once everything else is in place
    def connect_people
      read_file do |zip|
        transaction do
          Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet.new(account).connect_identities(from: zip)
          set_up_importer
          ensure_system_user
        end
      end
    end

    def set_up_importer
      user = account.users.find_by(identity: identity) ||
        account.users.create!(identity: identity, name: self.class.importer_name_for(identity), role: :owner, verified_at: Time.current)

      user.update!(role: :owner, active: true, verified_at: user.verified_at || Time.current)
      account.users.where(role: :owner).where.not(id: user.id).update_all(role: :admin)
      account.boards.all_access.find_each { |board| board.accesses.grant_to(user) }
    end

    def ensure_system_user
      unless account.users.exists?(role: :system)
        account.users.create!(role: :system, name: "System")
      end
    end

    def failure_reason_for(error)
      case error
      when Account::DataTransfer::ConflictError
        "#{error.message}. It looks like this account was already imported here."
      when Account::DataTransfer::Error
        error.message.end_with?(".") ? error.message : "#{error.message}."
      when ZipFile::Reader::InvalidArchive, ZipFile::Reader::EntryTooLarge, ZipFile::Reader::EntryNotFound
        "The file isn't a valid ZIP archive, or it's damaged."
      when ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
        "The uploaded file couldn't be found."
      else
        "Something went wrong on our end. Please try again, or contact support if the problem persists."
      end
    end

    def report(error)
      unless error.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::Error) || error.is_a?(ZipFile::Reader::InvalidArchive)
        Rails.error.report(error, severity: :error, context: { account_import_id: id })
      end
    end

    def roll_back
      if account
        Current.with_account(account) do
          manifest.delete_all
          file.purge
          account.incinerate
        end

        update!(account: nil)
      end
    end
end
EOF

# Imports an account in resumable steps. When the worker restarts, the import
# continues from the last batch of records it imported.
class Account::ImportJob < ApplicationJob
  include ActiveJob::Continuable

  queue_as :backend

  # A failed import is rolled back, so it must never be resumed
  self.resume_errors_after_advancing = false

  discard_on ActiveJob::DeserializationError

  def perform(import)
    if import.in_progress?
      step :check do |step|
        import.check start: step.cursor, callback: ->(cursor) { step.set! cursor }
      end

      step :import do |step|
        import.import start: step.cursor, callback: ->(cursor) { step.set! cursor }
      end

      step :reindex do |step|
        import.reindex start: step.cursor, callback: ->(cursor) { step.set! cursor }
      end

      step :finish do
        import.finish
      end
    end
  rescue => error
    import.fail(error)
  end
end

class Account::ImportsController < ApplicationController
  ZIP_SIGNATURES = [ "PK\x03\x04".b, "PK\x05\x06".b ].freeze

  disallow_account_scope

  rate_limit to: 5, within: 1.hour, only: :create, with: -> { redirect_to new_account_import_path, alert: "Too many imports. Please try again later." }

  before_action :ensure_accepting_imports, only: %i[ new create ]

  layout "public"

  def new
    @import = Account::Import.new
  end

  def create
    if zip_file?(file)
      @import = Account::Import.start(identity: Current.identity, file: file)
      redirect_to account_import_path(@import)
    else
      redirect_to new_account_import_path, alert: "Please choose a Fizzy account export, a .zip file."
    end
  rescue ActiveRecord::RecordNotSaved, ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid
    redirect_to new_account_import_path, alert: "Something went wrong, and we couldn't start your import. Please give it another try."
  end

  def show
    @import = Current.identity.account_imports.find(params[:id])
  end

  private
    def ensure_accepting_imports
      unless Account.accepting_signups?
        redirect_to session_menu_path, alert: "This Fizzy doesn't accept new accounts."
      end
    end

    def file
      params.dig(:account_import, :file)
    end

    def zip_file?(file)
      if file.respond_to?(:read)
        signature = file.read(4)
        file.rewind
        signature.present? && ZIP_SIGNATURES.include?(signature.b)
      end
    end
end
EOF

steps.message: Let me harden `Account::Import#fail` (idempotent, never rolls back a completed import), make stalled detection lenient, and keep the import "touched" during every step:
steps.reasoning_content:
I notice the stalled detection only touches updated_at during check/import steps but not during reindex or the final storage reconcile step, which could falsely flag long-running jobs as stalled. I should add a touch in the reindex callback too, and reconsider bumping STALLED_AFTER to account for edge cases like very large file uploads taking longer than expected.

I'm also worried about a race where the sweeper fails an import for exceeding STALLED_AFTER while the job is still actually running—this would cause `fail` to roll back the account while the job keeps inserting rows, potentially hitting a deleted account reference, triggering a rescue that calls `import.fail(error)` a second time and sends a duplicate email. I need to guard `fail` so it's a no-op if the import is already in a failed state, and make sure the job checks `in_progress?` status at multiple points, not just at the start.

Rather than fight the race condition directly, the simpler fix is to make it practically impossible: set STALLED_AFTER to something generous like a day, and have every step (check, import, reindex) touch the import every minute so a live job never looks stalled. I should also make `fail` idempotent, returning early if the import is already failed or completed, and think about whether `fail` getting called on a completed import causes problems.

require "active_job/test_helper"
require "active_job/continuation"

module ActiveJob
  class Continuation
    module TestHelper
      include ::ActiveJob::TestHelper

      def interrupt_job_during_step(job_class, step, cursor: nil, reason: true, &block)
        require_active_job_test_adapter!("interrupt_job_during_step")
        stopping = ->(job) { reason if job.is_a?(job_class) && during_step?(job, step, cursor: cursor) }
        queue_adapter.with(stopping: stopping, &block)
      end

      def interrupt_job_after_step(job_class, step, reason: true, &block)
        require_active_job_test_adapter!("interrupt_job_after_step")
        stopping = ->(job) { reason if job.is_a?(job_class) && after_step?(job, step) }
        queue_adapter.with(stopping: stopping, &block)
      end

      private
        def continuation_for(job)
          job.send(:continuation)&.to_h
        end

        def during_step?(job, step, cursor: nil)
          if (continuation = continuation_for(job))
            continuation["current"] == [ step.to_s, cursor ]
          end
        end

        def after_step?(job, step)
          if (continuation = continuation_for(job))
            continuation["completed"].last == step.to_s && continuation["current"].nil?
          end
        end
    end
  end
end

    def archive_for(files)

I'm planning the Account::Import test coverage: a full round-trip import into a fresh account verifying record counts, preserved IDs, files, rich text, mentions, ownership roles, reindexing, storage totals, and post-import behaviors like completion emails and sign-in; plus a conflict scenario ensuring failed imports leave no residual data.

Then I'm mapping out failure cases — missing account.json, corrupted ZIP, cross-account references in boards/blobs/files, broken rich text attachments referencing another account's blob — alongside success paths like an importer without existing user access getting a new owner, resuming interrupted imports, rolling back stalled ones, and creating identities for new people while cleaning up on duplicate-email failures.

I'm also working out the helper for wiping a source account via incineration plus blob purging, checking that `account.destroy` behaves correctly against the test fixture account as seen in the explore test.

I'm weighing whether leftover rows (like board events) could collide with reimported data, and deciding to write a `remove_account` helper combining manifest deletion and incineration to mirror the production rollback path before writing the actual import tests using the exported account fixture.

class Export < ApplicationRecord
  DOWNLOADABLE_FOR = 1.day
  STALLED_AFTER = 1.day
  KEPT_FOR = 1.month # So that old download links can tell they expired
  DAILY_LIMIT = 10

  belongs_to :account
  belongs_to :user

  has_one_attached :file, dependent: :purge_later

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  scope :in_progress, -> { where(status: %w[ pending processing ]) }
  scope :building, -> { in_progress.where(created_at: STALLED_AFTER.ago..) }
  scope :stalled, -> { in_progress.where(created_at: ...STALLED_AFTER.ago) }
  scope :expired, -> { completed.where(completed_at: ...DOWNLOADABLE_FOR.ago) }
  scope :recent, -> { where(created_at: 1.day.ago..) }

  class << self
    def cleanup
      expired.joins(:file_attachment).find_each { |export| export.file.purge }
      stalled.find_each(&:failed!)
      where(created_at: ...KEPT_FOR.ago).find_each(&:destroy)
    end

    def limit_reached_for?(user)
      where(user: user).recent.count >= DAILY_LIMIT
    end
  end

  def build_later
    Export::BuildJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def build
    processing!

    Current.with_account(account) do
      file.purge if file.attached?
      ZipFile.create_for(file, filename: filename) { |zip| populate_zip(zip) }
    end

    mark_completed
    ExportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later if user.identity.present?
  rescue => error
    failed! unless destroyed?
    raise error
  end

  def in_progress?
    pending? || processing?
  end

  def downloadable?
    completed? && !expired? && file.attached?
  end

  def expired?
    completed? && expires_at.past?
  end

  def expires_at
    completed_at + DOWNLOADABLE_FOR if completed_at
  end

  def accessible_to?(accessor)
    accessor.present? && accessor == user
  end

  def publicly_accessible?
    false
  end

  private
    def filename
      "fizzy-#{account.name.parameterize.presence || "account"}-#{created_at.utc.strftime("%Y%m%d%H%M")}.zip"
    end

    def mark_completed
      update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
    end

    def populate_zip(zip)
      raise NotImplementedError, "Subclasses must implement populate_zip"
    end
end

Good, the scratch directory isn't tracked since it's gitignored. For the intent-to-add entries I staged, I should run a plain git reset at the end so the index returns to its clean state, leaving those files untracked on disk rather than staged.

Now reviewing remaining design issues: RecordSet#import wraps work in model.transaction, which is fine for FilterRecordSet since its joins and inserts happen in the same transaction. But FileRecordSet performs blob uploads inside that same DB transaction, which is wasteful since it writes nothing to the database — though on SQLite a deferred transaction with no writes shouldn't actually hold a lock until a write occurs, so the long-running upload probably isn't blocking other writers after all.

I'm restructuring so the base import_batch handles the transaction around reference-checking and insertion, while FileRecordSet's import_batch skips the transaction entirely, and FilterRecordSet overrides import_batch to call super before inserting joins — accepting that a crash mid-batch just fails the whole import rather than resuming partially, since resumption only happens at batch checkpoints anyway.

Now I'm worrying about the FileRecordSet's batch size: 100 files per batch could mean 10GB uploaded between checkpoints, taking minutes, which conflicts with SolidQueue's default 5-second shutdown timeout on SIGTERM — if the job can't hit a checkpoint in that window, it gets killed mid-batch, and I need to figure out what happens to its claimed execution state in that case.

If a terminated worker's claimed execution gets released back to ready on restart, the job resumes from its last serialized checkpoint, which could be stale — leading to conflicts with already-imported records and confusing rollback failures during deploys. To fix this, I'm thinking I should shrink the checkpoint interval drastically for files (batch size 1) and lean on fast JSON record batches of 100, plus make the import steps idempotent so resumed jobs can tolerate re-processing already-imported rows instead of failing outright.

Using something like skip-duplicates-on-insert instead of a strict insert avoids re-crash failures, since the earlier check step already guarantees no conflicts against pre-existing data — so any duplicate during import can only come from our own prior partial attempt, not an external collision. But this raises a subtle security concern: skipping duplicates could silently skip a row whose ID happens to already exist under a different account, which isn't the behavior I want.

Now I'm checking how SolidQueue actually handles a crashed worker: claimed executions of dead processes get pruned and marked failed with ProcessPrunedError, while graceful shutdowns release them instead. So after a hard kill, the import job just fails outright rather than retrying, leaving it stuck "processing" until the sweeper eventually fails and rolls it back a day later—meaning resume isn't actually triggered in that scenario.

For a graceful release where the worker stops within the timeout but the job hasn't hit a checkpoint, SolidQueue puts the job back to ready and re-runs it from the last serialized continuation—skip-duplicates semantics would handle that fine since rows just get skipped and files get safely re-uploaded. That raises the question of whether I should always use insert_all with skip-duplicates, since doing so could mask a real ConflictError that the initial conflict check failed to catch.

I think I'd rather keep strict insert_all for normal first runs and only switch to skip-duplicates when resuming from a saved cursor, but the tricky case is when a release happens before any checkpoint is saved—then it reruns with the same nil `start` as a first run, hits strict mode, and could fail on a conflict that's actually just its own leftover rows from the aborted attempt. So instead I'm considering always skipping duplicates, but then verifying that any skipped rows actually belong to our own account—if they do, it's safe; if not, that's a genuine conflict and should raise an error.

Since `RETURNING` isn't supported on MySQL, I can't rely on insert_all's returned ids to check this. Instead I'll query existing ids in the batch beforehand, compare their account_id, raise a conflict if any belong to someone else, and then insert only the truly new rows with insert_all!—one cheap extra lookup per batch. Writing the insert method...

But I also need to think about other unique constraints beyond the primary key — blob keys, publication keys, (account_id, number) on cards, (user_id, card_id) on notifications — each of these could independently raise conflicts that this id-based check won't catch.

I realize HABTM join tables lack unique indexes, so re-running FilterRecordSet imports could duplicate join rows if filters were already inserted; I need to restructure so joins only get inserted for filters that are genuinely new, having `insert` return the newly inserted rows for FilterRecordSet to use. I also need to double check that the conflict check step doesn't misfire on resumed cursors where rows were already imported.

But there's a trickier failure mode: if a worker releases the job mid-import without checkpointing, re-running from scratch would hit the check step again, which would now find the partially-imported rows from the first attempt and incorrectly raise a ConflictError. I need check_conflicts to exclude rows that belong to our own account from that conflict detection.

Applying the same self-account exclusion to blob key conflicts makes the whole job properly idempotent. Going through each step—AccountRecordSet updates, EntropyRecordSet inserts, FileRecordSet re-uploads, connect_identities inside a transaction, reindexing, and reconcile_storage—they all hold up as re-runnable.

# Filters are exported along with the boards, tags and people they are scoped to.
class Account::DataTransfer::FilterRecordSet < Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  RESOURCES = %i[ tags boards assignees creators closers ].freeze

  def initialize(account)
    super(account: account, model: Filter)
  end

  def delete_all
    records.ids.each_slice(1000) do |filter_ids|
      RESOURCES.each { |resource| join_model_for(resource).where(filter_id: filter_ids).delete_all }
    end

    super
  end

  private
    def serialize(filter)
      super.merge(RESOURCES.to_h { |resource| [ resource_key(resource), filter.public_send(resource).ids ] })
    end

    def row_from(data)
      super.merge(RESOURCES.to_h { |resource| [ resource_key(resource), data[resource_key(resource)] ] })
    end

    def import_batch(entries)
      rows = entries.map { |entry| build_row(entry) }

      model.transaction do
        check_references(rows)

        inserted_ids = insert(rows.map { |row| row.except(*resource_keys) }).pluck("id").to_set
        rows.select { |row| inserted_ids.include?(row["id"]) }.each { |row| import_resources(row) }
      end
    end

    def import_resources(row)
      RESOURCES.each do |resource|
        ids = Array(row[resource_key(resource)]).uniq

        if ids.any?
          unless ids.all? { |id| valid_id?(id) }
            raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "Some filters reference invalid #{resource}"
          end

          reflection = Filter.reflect_on_association(resource)
          ensure_imported(reflection.klass, ids.to_set)
          join_model_for(resource).insert_all!(ids.map { |id| { "filter_id" => row["id"], reflection.association_foreign_key.to_s => id } })
        end
      end
    end

    def resource_keys
      RESOURCES.map { |resource| resource_key(resource) }
    end

    def resource_key(resource)
      "#{resource.to_s.singularize}_ids"
    end

    def join_model_for(resource)
      Filter.const_get("HABTM_#{resource.to_s.camelize}")
    end
end
EOF

{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Exports the records of a model into an archive, and checks and imports them back.
#
# Records keep their ids when imported, and are always imported into the target
# account. Before inserting each batch, every reference to another record is
# verified to point to a record that was already imported into the same account,
# so an archive can never be used to reach data in other accounts.
class Account::DataTransfer::RecordSet
  INTERNAL_RECORD_TYPES = %w[ Export Account::Import ].freeze

  # Polymorphic references are only allowed to point to these models
  REFERENCEABLE_TYPES = %w[
    Account Board Card Comment Event Mention User
    ActionText::RichText ActiveStorage::Blob ActiveStorage::VariantRecord
  ].freeze

  BATCH_SIZE = 100
  ID_FORMAT = /\A[0-9a-z]{25}\z/
  MAX_ID = 2**128

  attr_reader :account, :model, :attributes

  def initialize(account:, model:, attributes: nil)
    @account = account
    @model = model
    @attributes = (attributes || model.column_names).map(&:to_s)
  end

  # Identifies the record set in the cursors used to resume imports
  def name
    model_dir
  end

  def export(to:)
    with_zip(to) do
      each_record { |record| export_record(record) }
    end
  end

  # Validates the records in the archive without importing anything.
  def check(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      each_batch(start: start) do |entries|
        check_batch(entries)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: entries.last.path)
      end
    end
  end

  # Importing is idempotent, so an interrupted import can be resumed from any batch.
  def import(from:, start: nil, callback: nil)
    with_zip(from) do
      each_batch(start: start) do |entries|
        import_batch(entries)
        callback&.call(record_set: self, file: entries.last.path)
      end
    end
  end

  # Deletes everything of this kind in the account, to roll back a failed import.
  def delete_all
    records.in_batches(of: 1000).delete_all
  end

  private
    attr_reader :zip

    def with_zip(zip)
      old_zip = @zip
      @zip = zip
      yield
    ensure
      @zip = old_zip
    end

    def records
      model.where(account_id: account.id)
    end

    def model_dir
      model.table_name
    end

    # Exporting

    def each_record(&block)
      if records.respond_to?(:find_each)
        records.find_each(&block)
      else
        records.each(&block)
      end
    end

    def export_record(record)
      zip.add_file "data/#{model_dir}/#{record.id}.json", serialize(record).to_json
    end

    def serialize(record)
      record.attributes.slice(*attributes).transform_values do |value|
        value.respond_to?(:utc) ? value.utc.iso8601(6) : value
      end
    end

    # Importing

    def files
      zip.each_entry("data/#{model_dir}/*.json")
    end

    def each_batch(start:, &block)
      entries = files
      entries = entries_after(entries, start) if start
      entries.each_slice(batch_size, &block)
    end

    def batch_size
      BATCH_SIZE
    end

    def entries_after(entries, start)
      started = false

      Enumerator.new do |yielder|
        entries.each do |entry|
          if started
            yielder << entry
          else
            started = entry.path == start
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def check_batch(entries)
      check_conflicts entries.map { |entry| build_row(entry) }
    end

    def import_batch(entries)
      rows = entries.map { |entry| build_row(entry) }

      model.transaction do
        check_references(rows)
        insert(rows)
      end
    end

    def build_row(entry)
      data = load(entry)
      check_id(data, entry)

      row_from(data).tap do |row|
        check_values(row, entry)
      end
    end

    def load(entry)
      data = JSON.parse(zip.read(entry).force_encoding(Encoding::UTF_8))

      if data.is_a?(Hash)
        data
      else
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} doesn't contain a record"
      end
    rescue JSON::ParserError, EncodingError
      raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} isn't valid JSON"
    end

    def entry_path(entry)
      entry.respond_to?(:path) ? entry.path : entry
    end

    def row_from(data)
      attributes.index_with { |attribute| data.key?(attribute) ? data[attribute] : default_value_for(attribute) }.tap do |row|
        row["account_id"] = account.id if row.key?("account_id")
      end
    end

    def default_value_for(attribute)
      if attribute.in?(%w[ created_at updated_at ])
        Time.current
      else
        model.column_defaults[attribute]
      end
    end

    def check_id(data, entry)
      unless valid_id?(data["id"]) && File.basename(entry_path(entry), ".json") == data["id"]
        raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} doesn't have a valid id"
      end
    end

    def valid_id?(value)
      value.is_a?(String) && value.match?(ID_FORMAT) && value.to_i(36) < MAX_ID
    end

    def check_values(row, entry)
      uuid_attributes.each do |attribute|
        unless row[attribute].nil? || valid_id?(row[attribute])
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} has an invalid #{attribute}"
        end
      end

      model.defined_enums.each do |attribute, mapping|
        value = row[attribute]

        unless value.nil? || mapping.key?(value.to_s) || mapping.value?(value)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} has an invalid #{attribute}"
        end
      end

      polymorphic_references.each do |reflection|
        type = row[reflection.foreign_type]

        unless type.nil? || type.in?(REFERENCEABLE_TYPES)
          raise Account::DataTransfer::IntegrityError, "#{entry_path(entry)} references an unknown kind of record (#{type})"
        end
      end
    end

    def uuid_attributes
      @uuid_attributes ||= attributes.select do |attribute|
        model.type_for_attribute(attribute).is_a?(ActiveRecord::Type::Uuid)
      end
    end

    # Records already in the account were imported by an earlier attempt of the same import
    def check_conflicts(rows)
      if model.where(id: rows.pluck("id")).where.not(account_id: account.id).exists?
        raise Account::DataTransfer::ConflictError, "#{model.model_name.human.pluralize} in this file already exist in this Fizzy"
      end
    end

    def references
      model.reflect_on_all_associations(:belongs_to).reject do |reflection|
        reflection.name == :account || skipped_references.include?(reflection.name)
      end
    end

    def skipped_references
      []
    end

    def polymorphic_references
      references.select(&:polymorphic?)
    end

    # Ensures that every record referenced by the rows belongs to the account being imported
    def check_references(rows)
      referenced_ids(rows).each do |klass, ids|
        ensure_imported(klass, ids)
      end
    end

    def referenced_ids(rows)
      Hash.new { |hash, klass| hash[klass] = Set.new }.tap do |referenced|
        references.each do |reflection|
          rows.each do |row|
            if id = row[reflection.foreign_key.to_s]
              referenced[referenced_class(reflection, row)] << id
            end
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def referenced_class(reflection, row)

        reflection.klass
      elsif row[reflection.foreign_type].in?(REFERENCEABLE_TYPES)

      else

    end

    end

    # Inserts the rows that weren't imported yet, returning them.

results.content:
{
  "returncode": 0,
  "output": "# Imports an account export (see Account::Export) into a brand new account.
#
# The import runs in steps (see Account::ImportJob): the file is checked first,
# so most problems are caught before anything is written. Then the records and
# files are imported, the search index and storage totals are rebuilt and, at
# last, people are connected to their identities so they can sign in. Until
# then, nobody can access the new account.
#
# If anything goes wrong, everything imported is removed along with the new
# account, and the person importing gets an email explaining why.
class Account::Import < ApplicationRecord
  STALLED_AFTER = 1.day
  PROGRESS_INTERVAL = 1.minute

  belongs_to :account, optional: true
  belongs_to :identity

  has_one_attached :file

  enum :status, %w[ pending processing completed failed ].index_by(&:itself), default: :pending

  scope :in_progress, -> { where(status: %w[ pending processing ]) }
  scope :stalled, -> { in_progress.where(updated_at: ...STALLED_AFTER.ago) }

  validate :ensure_file_is_attached, on: :create

  class << self
    # Creates a new account for the identity and starts importing the file into it.
    def start(identity:, file:)
      signup = Signup.new(identity: identity, full_name: importer_name_for(identity), skip_account_seeding: true)

      if signup.complete
        create_for(signup.account, identity: identity, file: file).tap(&:process_later)
      else
        raise ActiveRecord::RecordNotSaved, signup.errors.full_messages.to_sentence
      end
    end

    def fail_stalled
      stalled.find_each do |import|
        import.fail Account::DataTransfer::Error.new("The import stopped making progress")
      end
    end

    def importer_name_for(identity)
      name = identity.users.where.not(name: identity.email_address).order(:updated_at).last&.name
      (name.presence || identity.email_address.split("@").first).truncate(240)
    end

    private
      def create_for(account, identity:, file:)
        Current.with_account(account) do
          # Nobody can get into the account until it has been imported
          account.users.destroy_all
          create!(account: account, identity: identity, file: file)
        end
      rescue
        account.destroy
        raise
      end
  end

  def process_later
    Account::ImportJob.perform_later(self)
  end

  def check(start: nil, callback: nil)
    processing! if pending?

    each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, zip, last_file|
      record_set.check(from: zip, start: last_file, callback: progress_callback(callback))
    end
  end

  def import(start: nil, callback: nil)
    each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, zip, last_file|
      record_set.import(from: zip, start: last_file, callback: progress_callback(callback))
    end
  end

  def reindex(start: nil, callback: nil)
    Current.with_account(account) do
      reindex_cards(start: start, callback: callback)
      reindex_comments(start: start, callback: callback)
    end
  end

  def finish
    Current.with_account(account) do
      reconcile_account
      connect_people

      file.purge
      update!(status: :completed, completed_at: Time.current)
    end

    ImportMailer.completed(self).deliver_later
  end

  # Removes everything imported along with the new account, and lets the person
  # importing know why the import failed.
  def fail(error)
    report(error)

    if in_progress?
      update!(status: :failed, failure_reason: failure_reason_for(error))
      roll_back
      ImportMailer.failed(self).deliver_later
    end
  end

  def in_progress?
    pending? || processing?
  end

  private
    def ensure_file_is_attached
      errors.add(:file, "is missing") unless file.attached?
    end

    def manifest
      Account::DataTransfer::Manifest.new(account)
    end

    def each_record_set(start: nil)
      Current.with_account(account) do
        read_file do |zip|
          manifest.each_record_set(start: start) do |record_set, last_file|
            yield record_set, zip, last_file
          end
        end
      end
    end

    def read_file(&block)
      ZipFile.read_from(file.blob, &block)
    end

    # Reports the position of the import, so that it can be resumed from there if interrupted
    def progress_callback(callback)
      lambda do |record_set:, file:|
        report_progress([ record_set.name, file ], callback)
      end
    end

    def report_progress(cursor, callback)
      touch if updated_at < PROGRESS_INTERVAL.ago
      callback&.call(cursor)
    end

    def reindex_cards(start:, callback:)
      if start.nil? || start.first == "cards"
        account.cards.published.includes(:rich_text_description).find_each(start: start&.last) do |card|
          card.reindex
          report_progress([ "cards", card.id ], callback)
        end
      end
    end

    def reindex_comments(start:, callback:)
      comments_start = start.last if start&.first == "comments"

      Comment.where(account: account).joins(:card).merge(Card.published).includes(:rich_text_body, :card).find_each(start: comments_start) do |comment|
        comment.reindex
        report_progress([ "comments", comment.id ], callback)
      end
    end

    def reconcile_account
      account.update!(cards_count: [ account.cards_count, account.cards.maximum(:number).to_i ].max)

      account.boards.find_each do |board|
        board.reconcile_storage
        board.materialize_storage
      end

      account.reconcile_storage
      account.materialize_storage
    end

    # Identities are global, so people are connected to them only once everything else is in place
    def connect_people
      read_file do |zip|
        transaction do
          Account::DataTransfer::UserRecordSet.new(account).connect_identities(from: zip)
          set_up_importer
          ensure_system_user
        end
      end
    end

    def set_up_importer
      user = account.users.find_by(identity: identity) ||
        account.users.create!(identity: identity, name: self.class.importer_name_for(identity), role: :owner, verified_at: Time.current)

      user.update!(role: :owner, active: true, verified_at: user.verified_at || Time.current)
      account.users.where(role: :owner).where.not(id: user.id).update_all(role: :admin)
      account.boards.all_access.find_each { |board| board.accesses.grant_to(user) }
    end

    def ensure_system_user
      unless account.users.exists?(role: :system)
        account.users.create!(role: :system, name: "System")
      end
    end

    def failure_reason_for(error)
      case error
      when Account::DataTransfer::ConflictError
        "This file contains data that already exists in this Fizzy. That happens when the account it was exported from, or an earlier import of it, is still here."
      when Account::DataTransfer::Error
        error.message.end_with?(".") ? error.message : "#{error.message}."
      when ZipFile::Reader::InvalidArchive, ZipFile::Reader::EntryTooLarge, ZipFile::Reader::EntryNotFound
        "The file isn't a valid ZIP archive, or it's damaged."
      when ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError
        "The uploaded file couldn't be found."
      else
        "Something went wrong on our end. Please try again, or contact support if the problem persists."
      end
    end

    def report(error)
      unless error.is_a?(Account::DataTransfer::Error) || error.is_a?(ZipFile::Reader::InvalidArchive)
        Rails.error.report(error, severity: :error, context: { account_import_id: id })
      end
    end

    def roll_back
      if account
        Current.with_account(account) do
          Storage::Total.where(owner_type: "Board", owner_id: account.boards.select(:id)).delete_all
          manifest.delete_all
          file.purge
          account.reload.incinerate
        end

        update!(account: nil)
      end
    end
end
"
}

class ZipFile::Reader
  class InvalidArchive < StandardError; end
  class EntryNotFound < StandardError; end
  class EntryTooLarge < StandardError; end

  def glob(pattern)

  def each_entry(pattern = "*")

    literal_prefix = pattern[/\A[^*?\[{\\]*/]

          yield relative(entry) if File.fnmatch(pattern, entry.path)
        end
      end
    end
  end

  # Returns the full contents of the entry, or streams them in chunks when given a block.
  def read(path_or_entry, max_size: MAX_READ_SIZE)
    entry = entry_for(path_or_entry)

    if block_given?
      open(entry) { |io| io.each_chunk { |chunk| yield chunk } }
    elsif entry.size > max_size
      raise EntryTooLarge, "#{entry.path} is too large (#{entry.size} bytes)"
    else
      open(entry) { |io| io.read }
    end
  end

  # Yields an IO-like object (responding to +read+, +size+ and +rewind+) with the entry contents.
  def open(path_or_entry)
    yield EntryIO.new(self, entry_for(path_or_entry))
  end

    @io.seek(data_offset_for(entry), IO::SEEK_SET)
